description: User-authoritative narration for the exact ten-page 1945 Remember When PDF. The complete SHA-256 and page count must match before any text is used.

pages.1: 1945. Remember When. A nostalgic look back in time.
pages.2: Remember When, 1945. To Dad. From Dan and Diana. Date: August seventh, twenty twenty-six. The richness of life lies in the memories we have forgotten.
pages.3:
1945 Timeline.

January: Pepe Le Pew debuts in the Warner Brothers cartoon, Odor-able Kitty.

February: Walt Disney's The Three Caballeros opens in New York.

March: Phyllis M. Daley is the first Black nurse sworn in as a United States Navy ensign.

April: The National Football League requires players to wear long stockings.

May: Arthur C. Clarke proposes relay satellites in geosynchronous orbit.

June: The Charter of the United Nations is signed.

July: A United States Army bomber crashes into the seventy-ninth floor of the Empire State Building.

August: In Washington, the thirty-five mile-per-hour speed limit ends.

September: The United States regains possession of Wake Island from Japan.

October: Jackie Robinson is chosen to integrate baseball and signs with the Montreal Royals, the top Dodgers farm team.

November: The first issue of Ebony magazine is published by John H. Johnson.

December: The microwave oven is patented.
pages.4:
1945 World News.

Italian partisans kill Benito Mussolini.

After destroying major cities in Germany, Hitler commits suicide.

World War Two comes to an end, May eighth in Europe, and August fourteenth in the Pacific, after involving fifty-seven nations. Fifty-five million people died.

Soviet troops liberate prisoners of the concentration camp at Auschwitz. Several million people died during the course of the Holocaust, both in and out of German camps.

The American flag is raised over Iwo Jima.

The United Nations convenes with representatives from fifty-one nations.
pages.5:
1945 National News.

Harry Truman takes the office of President after Roosevelt passes away.

Japanese Americans are permitted to return to the West Coast.

The United Auto Workers strike against General Motors for one hundred thirteen days.

Grand Rapids, Michigan, is the first United States community to fluoridate water.

In 1945, five thousand homes have television sets.

Ballpoint pens, Tupperware, and frozen orange juice all hit the market.

United States Army General George S. Patton passes away.

President of the United States: Franklin Roosevelt, then Harry Truman.

Vice President of the United States: Harry Truman, then none.

Pulitzer Prize winner: A Bell for Adano, by John Hersey.

Nobel Peace Prize winner: Cordell Hull.

Miss America: Bess Myerson, of New York, New York.

Speaker of the House of Representatives: Sam T. Rayburn, Democrat.

Canadian Prime Minister: William Lyon Mackenzie King.

Life expectancy: sixty-two point nine years.

Remember when. Popular radio shows in 1945 included Break the Bank, Meet the Press, and Green Hornet.
pages.7:
1945 Cost of Living.

Living.

New house: four thousand six hundred twenty-five dollars.

Average income: two thousand three hundred ninety dollars per year.

New car: one thousand twenty-five dollars.

Average rent: sixty dollars per month.

Tuition to Harvard University: four hundred twenty dollars per year.

Movie ticket: fifty cents each.

Gasoline: fifteen cents per gallon.

First-class postage stamp: three cents each.

Food.

Granulated sugar: seventy-five cents for ten pounds.

Vitamin D milk: sixty-two cents per gallon.

Ground coffee: fifty cents per pound.

Bacon: forty-five cents per pound.

Eggs: twenty-two cents per dozen.

Fresh ground hamburger: thirty-five cents per pound.

Fresh baked bread: nine cents per loaf.
pages.8:
1945 Birth Notices.

Bette Midler. December first. Bette Davis Midler was born in Honolulu, Hawaii. She studied drama at the University of Hawaii. In 1972, she recorded her platinum debut, The Divine Miss M. Midler is also a successful actress. Some of her movies include The Rose, Boys on the Side, and Down and Out in Beverly Hills.

Sir Van Morrison. August thirty-first. Belfast-born George Ivan Morrison received his first guitar when he was twelve. The Grammy winner's tunes include Moondance, Brown Eyed Girl, and Into the Mystic. The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducted him in 1993. He was knighted in 2016 for his contributions to music and tourism in Northern Ireland.

Goldie Hawn. November twenty-first. Goldie Jeanne Hawn was born in Washington, D.C. She first found fame on Rowan and Martin's Laugh-In. Hawn won an Oscar for her first major movie, Cactus Flower. After the sixties, she both starred in and produced numerous hits, including Shampoo, The First Wives Club, and Private Benjamin.

January twenty-ninth: Tom Selleck, actor.

February ninth: Mia Farrow, entertainer.

March thirtieth: Eric Clapton, guitarist and singer.

June twentieth: Anne Murray, singer.

October thirtieth: Henry Winkler, actor.

United States Open Golf winner: The United States Open was not held in 1945.

Pro Football champion: Cleveland Rams.

Indianapolis Five Hundred winner: The Indianapolis Five Hundred was not held in 1945.

Stanley Cup winner: Toronto Maple Leafs.

National Collegiate Athletic Association Basketball champion: Oklahoma A and M.

College Football champion: Army.

Heisman Trophy winner: Felix Blanchard, from Army.

Remember when. Pete Gray, a one-armed outfielder pressed into action because of the World War Two manpower shortage, plays seventy-seven games and bats point two one eight for the Saint Louis Browns in his first and only year in the major leagues.
